questions.stem: Determine the name of the following piece of lab equipment: A shallow dish used for evaporating liquids.

options.A: Crucible
options.B: Beaker
options.C: Evaporating dish
options.D: Watch glass

questions.explanation: An evaporating dish is a shallow porcelain dish used to concentrate or evaporate solutions to dryness.

questions.stem: Determine the name of the following piece of lab equipment: A conical-shaped device used to direct liquid or powder into a small opening.

options.A: Buret
options.B: Funnel
options.C: Watch glass
options.D: Well plate

questions.explanation: A funnel has a wide cone and narrow stem, used to channel liquids or powders into containers with small openings.

questions.stem: What is the best instrument for accurately measuring and delivering variable volumes of liquid during titrations?

options.A: Beaker
options.B: Erlenmeyer flask
options.C: Buret
options.D: Evaporating dish

questions.explanation: A buret (burette) is the only instrument that can accurately measure AND deliver variable volumes (±0.05 cm³) with its stopcock.

questions.stem: Determine the name of the following piece of lab equipment: A tall, narrow, graduated glass tube used for precise volume measurement.

options.A: Buret
options.B: Beaker
options.C: Erlenmeyer flask
options.D: Graduated cylinder

questions.explanation: A graduated cylinder is marked with precise volume graduations and is used for measuring liquid volumes more accurately than a beaker.

questions.stem: Determine the name of the following piece of lab equipment: A conical flask with a flat bottom and narrow neck, used for mixing and heating.

options.A: Beaker
options.B: Graduated cylinder
options.C: Buret
options.D: Erlenmeyer flask

questions.explanation: The Erlenmeyer (conical) flask has a wide base and narrow neck, making it ideal for swirling liquids during titrations without spilling.

questions.stem: Selection of filter paper depends on the size of particles to be ________.

options.A: filtered
options.B: dried
options.C: decolorized
options.D: decanted

questions.explanation: Filter paper pore size is chosen based on the size of the particles to be filtered — coarser particles use larger pore size paper.

questions.stem: Which of the following separation techniques is dependent on difference in volatility?

options.A: Distillation
options.B: Crystallization
options.C: Magnetic separation
options.D: Fractional crystallization

questions.explanation: Distillation separates mixtures based on differences in boiling points (volatility). The more volatile component evaporates first.

questions.stem: Crystallization exploits difference in which factors?

options.A: Specific heat
options.B: Boiling point
options.C: Melting point
options.D: Bubble point

questions.explanation: Crystallization exploits differences in solubility at different temperatures — cooling a hot saturated solution causes less-soluble material to crystallize out.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods is applied to separate Oxygen-rich and Nitrogen-rich components from liquid air?

options.A: Crystallization
options.B: Zone melting
options.C: Magnetic separation
options.D: Distillation

questions.explanation: Fractional distillation of liquid air separates O₂ (b.p. -183°C) and N₂ (b.p. -196°C) based on their different boiling points.

questions.stem: How are Oil and Hexane separated?

options.A: Distillation
options.B: Separating funnel
options.C: Crystallization
options.D: Electrophoresis

questions.explanation: Oil and hexane are immiscible liquids that form separate layers. A separating funnel allows the denser layer to be drained off independently.

questions.stem: When do we use a Buffer Solution?

options.A: To make the solution basic
options.B: To make the solution acidic
options.C: To prevent solution's pH change
options.D: None of the above

questions.explanation: A buffer solution resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added, maintaining a relatively constant pH.

questions.stem: What type of indicator is Chlorophenol Red?

options.A: Redox indicator
options.B: Colorimetric indicator
options.C: Adsorption indicator
options.D: Radioactive indicator

questions.explanation: Chlorophenol Red is a pH colorimetric indicator that changes colour based on the hydrogen ion concentration of the solution.

questions.stem: What is the colour of the Phenolsulfonphthalein (Phenol Red) indicator at pH 7.0?

options.A: Red
options.B: Violet
options.C: Green
options.D: Yellow

questions.explanation: Phenol Red (Phenolsulfonphthalein) appears yellow below pH 6.8, orange-red at neutral pH 7, and bright pink/red above pH 8.4.

questions.stem: Why does the colour of [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ solution appear red?

options.A: Complex adds red radiation to solvent
options.B: Absorbs in the complementary green region and transmits red component
options.C: Absorbs in the red region
options.D: None of the above

questions.explanation: The Fe(SCN)²⁺ complex absorbs green light (complementary colour) and transmits red light, which is what we perceive as the red colour.

questions.stem: What is the correct statement for a 'reducing agent'?

options.A: It has a higher oxidation state
options.B: It withdraws electrons
options.C: It reduces oxidising agents by donating electrons
options.D: It gets reduced itself in the redox reaction

questions.explanation: A reducing agent donates electrons to other species (oxidising agents), causing them to be reduced. The reducing agent itself gets oxidised.

questions.stem: In photosynthesis, water is oxidised into ____________.

options.A: H₂
options.B: CO₂
options.C: C₆H₁₂O₆
options.D: O₂

questions.explanation: In photosynthesis, water molecules are split (oxidised) by light energy: 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ + O₂. The oxygen is released as a byproduct.

questions.stem: What is the potential value of the standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) at 298K?
questions.explanation: By international convention, the standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) is assigned a standard electrode potential of exactly 0 V at all temperatures.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods can be used to separate a mixture of iron and copper fillings?

options.A: Magnetic separation
options.B: Crystallisation
options.C: Evaporation
options.D: Distillation

questions.explanation: Iron is ferromagnetic and is attracted to a magnet, while copper is non-magnetic. A magnet easily separates the two metals.

questions.stem: Which separation method is used to separate solutes that all dissolve in the same solvent?

options.A: Evaporation
options.B: Filtration
options.C: Chromatography
options.D: Sublimation

questions.explanation: Chromatography separates mixtures of solutes dissolved in the same solvent based on their different affinities for the stationary and mobile phases.

questions.stem: A mixture of oil and water is separated by ____.

options.A: Separating funnel
options.B: Evaporation
options.C: Decantation
options.D: Filtration

questions.explanation: Oil and water are immiscible. They form two distinct layers in a separating funnel, allowing each layer to be drained separately.

questions.stem: Which method of separation will be used to separate butter from curd?

options.A: Sublimation
options.B: Chromatography
options.C: Centrifugation
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Centrifugation uses centrifugal force to separate components of different densities. Butter (less dense fat) separates from curd (denser liquid).

questions.stem: The process in which heavier impurities settle at the bottom of a liquid is ____.

options.A: Decantation
options.B: Sedimentation
options.C: Filtration
options.D: Evaporation

questions.explanation: Sedimentation is the process where suspended particles settle to the bottom under gravity due to their higher density compared to the liquid.

questions.stem: What piece of equipment dispenses liquids in measured drops?

options.A: Pipette
options.B: Dropper
options.C: Beaker
options.D: Flask

questions.explanation: A dropper (also called a Pasteur pipette or medicine dropper) dispenses liquids one drop at a time for precise small volume addition.

questions.stem: What piece of equipment is used for stirring, mixing, heating, and rough measurements of liquids?

options.A: Beaker
options.B: Flask
options.C: Dropper
options.D: Mortar and pestle

questions.explanation: A beaker is a general-purpose cylindrical container used for mixing, heating, and rough volume measurement. It is NOT for accurate volumetric measurements.

questions.stem: What piece of equipment is used to hold test tubes upright?

options.A: Test tube rack
options.B: Forceps
options.C: Ring clamp
options.D: Petri dish

questions.explanation: A test tube rack holds multiple test tubes in an upright position, preventing them from rolling or falling during experiments.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the simplest member of organic compounds?

options.A: Formic acid
options.B: Formaldehyde
options.C: Methane
options.D: Methanol

questions.explanation: Methane (CH₄) is the simplest alkane and the simplest organic compound, consisting of one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms.

questions.stem: Hydrocarbons are organic compounds containing element(s) ________.

options.A: Both hydrogen and carbon
options.B: Carbon only
options.C: Hydrogen only
options.D: Oxygen

questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons by definition contain ONLY hydrogen and carbon atoms. Examples include methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), and benzene (C₆H₆).

questions.stem: Ammonia evolved from 0.75 g soil sample neutralises 10 mL of 1M H₂SO₄ in Kjeldahl's method. Find the percentage of nitrogen in the soil.
questions.explanation: Moles H₂SO₄ = 0.01×1 = 0.01 mol. Moles NH₃ = 0.02 mol (1 mol H₂SO₄ reacts with 2 mol NH₃). Mass N = 0.02×14 = 0.28 g. %N = (0.28/0.75)×100 = 37.33%.

questions.stem: 25 mL of barium hydroxide solution titrated against 0.1 M HCl gave titer of 35 mL. What is the molarity of Ba(OH)₂?
With increase in temperature, which of these changes?

options.A: Molality
options.B: Fraction of solute present in water
options.C: Weight fraction of solute
options.D: Mole fraction

questions.explanation: Molality, mole fraction, and mass fraction are all temperature-independent. Molarity changes with temperature, and weight fraction of solute can change as density changes with temperature.

questions.stem: Which piece of apparatus is specifically designed for evaporating liquid solutions to dryness or concentrating them?

options.A: Evaporating dish — shallow porcelain dish with a spout; can be heated directly
options.B: Beaker — cylindrical flat-bottomed glass vessel used for mixing
options.C: Crucible — small deep container for igniting at very high temperatures
options.D: Watch glass — thin circular glass plate used as a cover

questions.explanation: The evaporating dish is made of porcelain and can be heated directly on a wire gauze. Its shallow design allows rapid evaporation of solvent.

questions.stem: A burette is a long graduated glass tube with a stopcock. What is its PRIMARY function in laboratory titrations?

options.A: Measuring approximate volumes of liquid for rough experiments
options.B: Accurately measuring and delivering variable volumes during titrations (up to 50.00 cm³ ±0.05 cm³)
options.C: Transferring a fixed definite volume from a stock solution
options.D: Storing concentrated acid reagents safely between experiments

questions.explanation: The burette with its stopcock allows precise control of liquid flow and can deliver any volume from 0 to 50 cm³ with ±0.05 cm³ accuracy.

questions.stem: A Bunsen burner is the most common heating device in the general chemistry laboratory. It burns what type of fuel gas?

options.A: Hydrogen gas (H₂) from a cylinder
options.B: Oxygen gas (O₂) under pressure
options.C: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) — propane or butane
options.D: Carbon monoxide (CO) piped from the main line

questions.explanation: Bunsen burners typically use LPG (propane/butane) or natural gas (methane) as fuel. The air-gas ratio is adjusted via the air hole to control flame type.

questions.stem: What is the beehive shelf used for in a gas preparation set-up involving collection over water?

options.A: To hold hot crucibles safely after ignition
options.B: To support the Bunsen burner and tripod stand
options.C: To support the inverted gas jar at the right height in a pneumatic trough for displacement collection
options.D: To hold folded filter paper flat during gravity filtration

questions.explanation: The beehive shelf sits in the pneumatic trough and has a hole through which gas travels upward into the inverted water-filled gas jar.

questions.stem: What is the crucible primarily used for in the chemistry laboratory?

options.A: Measuring volumes of liquids accurately to 0.01 cm³
options.B: Supporting filter paper during gravity filtration
options.C: Holding solid substances being heated or ignited to very high temperatures until they decompose
options.D: Dissolving solid chemicals in a liquid solvent at room temperature

questions.explanation: Crucibles are made of porcelain, clay, or platinum and can withstand extremely high temperatures needed for ignition and decomposition reactions.

questions.stem: A mortar and pestle (porcelain or agate) are used for what specific purpose in the chemistry laboratory?

options.A: Measuring the pH of a solution accurately
options.B: Grinding and crushing solid chemicals into a fine, homogeneous powder
options.C: Holding liquid reagents at constant high temperatures for extended reactions
options.D: Mixing two immiscible liquid phases by mechanical agitation

questions.explanation: The pestle is used to crush and grind solids in the bowl (mortar), increasing surface area for faster dissolution or reaction.

questions.stem: A wire gauze with a ceramic/asbestos centre is placed on a tripod stand. What is its purpose?

options.A: To filter fine solid particles from a liquid suspension
options.B: To collect gases over water by displacement in a trough
options.C: To support a vessel (beaker, flask, dish) and distribute heat evenly from the Bunsen burner below
options.D: To weigh solid chemicals accurately on an analytical balance

questions.explanation: The ceramic centre of the wire gauze spreads heat from the Bunsen flame uniformly, preventing hot spots that could crack glassware.

questions.stem: A retort stand with a clamp is used to support which apparatus during laboratory experiments?

options.A: The Bunsen burner and tripod stand only
options.B: The filter funnel, thermometer, burette, condenser, or flask — whichever requires vertical support
options.C: The evaporating dish during crystallisation only
options.D: The mortar and pestle during grinding operations

questions.explanation: The retort stand with boss and clamp is a versatile support system for virtually any piece of apparatus requiring vertical or angled positioning.

questions.stem: A test-tube holder is specifically designed for what purpose?

options.A: Holding test tubes upright in a rack when not in use
options.B: Safely gripping hot test tubes or those containing corrosive and reactive reagents
options.C: Measuring the exact volume of liquid inside a test tube
options.D: Sealing a test tube tightly to prevent escape of gas

questions.explanation: Test-tube holders allow the experimenter to handle test tubes safely during heating without burning their fingers or dropping the tube.

questions.stem: What is the key difference between a measuring cylinder and a burette when measuring liquid volumes?

options.A: A measuring cylinder is more accurate than a burette in all situations
options.B: They are identical — 'burette' is just an alternative name for a measuring cylinder
options.C: A burette (±0.05 cm³) is far more accurate than a measuring cylinder (±0.5 mL); only the burette has a stopcock for controlled delivery
options.D: A measuring cylinder has a stopcock; a burette does not

questions.explanation: A burette is a precision instrument with 10× better accuracy than a measuring cylinder and is used in quantitative titration analysis.

questions.stem: The Hofmann voltameter is used in the laboratory for which specific purpose?

options.A: Measuring the electromotive force (EMF) of a galvanic cell
options.B: Electrolyzing water to produce and separately collect hydrogen (cathode) and oxygen (anode) in graduated tubes
options.C: Testing electrical conductivity of dilute ionic solutions
options.D: Separating charged molecules by electrophoresis on a gel plate

questions.explanation: The Hofmann voltameter demonstrates the electrolysis of water: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. H₂ collects at the cathode (twice the volume of O₂ at the anode).

questions.stem: Simple distillation separates components based on which physical property?

options.A: Difference in density of the two liquids
options.B: Difference in volatility (boiling point) — the more volatile component evaporates and is condensed and collected first
options.C: Difference in solubility in a common third solvent
options.D: Difference in magnetic susceptibility of the components

questions.explanation: Simple distillation works best when boiling points differ by more than 25°C. The lower boiling point component distils over first.

questions.stem: Fractional distillation of ethanol (b.p. 78°C) and water (b.p. 100°C) requires which additional apparatus compared to simple distillation?

options.A: A separating funnel to drain off the denser layer
options.B: A fractionating column packed with glass beads — providing multiple condensation/re-evaporation cycles for better separation
options.C: A Buchner funnel and vacuum pump for suction filtration
options.D: A chromatographic tank with solvent and silica stationary phase

questions.explanation: The fractionating column provides many theoretical plates where vapour repeatedly condenses and re-evaporates, giving better separation of close-boiling components.

questions.stem: Crystallisation as a separation technique exploits what physical property of the dissolved substance?

options.A: Difference in specific heat capacity between solute and solvent
options.B: Difference in boiling points at standard atmospheric pressure
options.C: Difference in solubility at different temperatures — cooling a hot saturated solution causes less-soluble material to crystallise out
options.D: Difference in bubble-point pressure at reduced atmospheric pressure

questions.explanation: Most solids are more soluble at high temperatures. Rapid cooling of a saturated solution produces crystals of the pure substance.

questions.stem: Which method is used to separate a mixture of immiscible liquids such as kerosene and water?

options.A: Separating funnel — the two immiscible liquids form separate density-based layers that can be drained independently
options.B: Evaporation — the water evaporates, leaving the kerosene
options.C: Filtration — using filter paper to trap the kerosene
options.D: Simple distillation — the liquids are boiled and condensed separately

questions.explanation: Kerosene (less dense, upper layer) and water (denser, lower layer) separate by density. The stopcock allows each layer to be drained independently.

questions.stem: How are a mixture of iron filings and copper filings best separated?

options.A: Magnetic separation — iron is ferromagnetic and attracted by a magnet; copper is non-magnetic
options.B: Crystallisation from a common solvent at low temperature
options.C: Evaporation from a mixed dissolved metallic solution
options.D: Distillation from a mixed metallic melt

questions.explanation: Iron's ferromagnetism makes it respond strongly to magnetic fields. Copper, being diamagnetic, is not attracted by a magnet.

questions.stem: Which separation method is used to separate several solutes that all dissolve in the same solvent?

options.A: Evaporation to dryness — removes only the solvent
options.B: Gravity filtration — separates only insoluble solids
options.C: Chromatography — different solutes migrate at different rates through the stationary phase with the mobile phase solvent
options.D: Sublimation — applicable only when one component sublimes

questions.explanation: Chromatography separates solutes based on their differential affinity for the stationary phase vs. the mobile phase, giving different migration distances (Rf values).

questions.stem: The process in which heavier suspended impurities settle at the bottom of a liquid under gravity is called:

options.A: Decantation
options.B: Sedimentation
options.C: Filtration
options.D: Evaporation

questions.explanation: Sedimentation is the gravitational settling of dense particles. Decantation is the subsequent pouring off of the clear liquid above the sediment.

questions.stem: If a laboratory fire breaks out involving a burning organic solvent, what should be done FIRST?

options.A: Pour water directly onto the flame to extinguish it quickly
options.B: Smother the fire with a fire blanket or damp cloth — water can spread burning organic liquid and worsen the fire
options.C: Blow out the flame with a fan directed at the burning liquid
options.D: Immediately leave the lab and do not attempt to extinguish it

questions.explanation: Water floats organic solvents and spreads the fire. Smothering cuts off the oxygen supply. Always use CO₂ extinguisher or fire blanket for solvent fires.

questions.stem: What Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is essential in the chemistry laboratory at all times?

options.A: Only a lab coat to protect clothing from spills
options.B: Only safety goggles to protect the eyes from splashes
options.C: Laboratory coat, safety goggles, and closed-toe shoes — at minimum; gloves when handling corrosive, toxic, or carcinogenic substances
options.D: No PPE is required for simple, room-temperature experiments

questions.explanation: The minimum PPE in any chemistry lab are lab coat (body protection), safety goggles (eye protection), and closed shoes (foot protection from spills and broken glass).

questions.stem: What does the COSHH acronym stand for in laboratory safety?

options.A: Chemical Operations Safe Substance Handling
options.B: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health
options.C: Certified Operations for Safe Substance Handling in Hospitals
options.D: Chemical Oversight for Safety and Substance Handling

questions.explanation: COSHH (Control of Substances Hazardous to Health) is the regulatory framework requiring risk assessment and safe handling procedures for hazardous chemicals.

questions.stem: Why is Teflon (PTFE) used for stopcock plugs, tubing, and seals in laboratory apparatus?

options.A: Because it is transparent and allows colour changes to be observed easily
options.B: Because it is the cheapest and most available polymer material
options.C: Because it is chemically inert to virtually all common chemicals including strong acids, bases, and organic solvents
options.D: Because it is an excellent conductor of heat and electricity

questions.explanation: PTFE (Teflon) has exceptional chemical resistance due to strong C-F bonds that resist attack by virtually all laboratory chemicals, making it ideal for seals and stopcocks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the simplest member of all organic compounds?

options.A: Formic acid (HCOOH) — the simplest carboxylic acid
options.B: Formaldehyde (HCHO) — the simplest aldehyde
options.C: Methane (CH₄) — the simplest alkane, hydrocarbon, and organic compound
options.D: Methanol (CH₃OH) — the simplest alcohol

questions.explanation: Methane (CH₄) has just one carbon and four hydrogens. It is the first member of the alkane homologous series and the simplest of all organic compounds.

questions.stem: The Liebig condenser consists of an inner glass tube and an outer glass jacket. What is its function in distillation?

options.A: To increase the boiling point of the liquid being distilled
options.B: To cool and condense vapour from the flask into liquid distillate using cold water flowing through the outer jacket
options.C: To separate gases by molecular weight in a density gradient
options.D: To precisely measure the temperature of the boiling liquid

questions.explanation: The Liebig condenser uses flowing cold water in the outer jacket to cool and condense vapour passing through the inner tube, converting it back to liquid distillate.

questions.stem: A Buchner funnel is made of perforated porcelain. When connected to a Buchner flask and vacuum pump, what process does it enable?

options.A: Simple gravity filtration using folded filter paper in a conical funnel
options.B: Fractional distillation of close-boiling liquid mixtures
options.C: Filtration under suction (reduced pressure), which is faster and leaves the solid drier
options.D: Intermittent supply of liquid acid reagents to a reaction mixture

questions.explanation: Vacuum filtration through a Buchner funnel is 10× faster than gravity filtration and produces much drier filter cakes — essential for collecting crystalline products.

questions.stem: To accurately measure and transfer exactly 25.0 cm³ of a liquid for a titration, which apparatus should be used?

options.A: A 100 mL measuring cylinder read to the nearest 0.5 mL
options.B: A 250 mL conical flask filled to a graduation mark
options.C: A 25 cm³ bulb (transfer) pipette calibrated to deliver precisely 25.00 cm³
options.D: A 50 mL beaker with printed graduation marks

questions.explanation: A bulb (one-mark) pipette delivers exactly one fixed volume with the highest accuracy (±0.04 cm³), far superior to measuring cylinders or beakers.

questions.stem: Why is a round-bottomed flask (RBF) preferred over a flat-bottomed flask for distillation and reflux?

options.A: Because it is cheaper and more readily available than flat-bottomed flasks
options.B: Because it holds more liquid than a flat-bottomed flask of the same size
options.C: Because the curved surface distributes heat evenly and prevents the glass from cracking under thermal stress
options.D: Because it can be stoppered more easily with a rubber bung

questions.explanation: Curved glassware distributes thermal stress evenly. Flat-bottomed flasks concentrate stress at corners and can crack when heated strongly.

questions.stem: A thistle funnel has a bulb top and a long, narrow stem. What is it used for in gas preparation?

options.A: Filtering solid impurities from a liquid solvent
options.B: Adding a liquid reagent (acid) to a solid inside a flask, allowing controlled introduction while sealing the apparatus
options.C: Separating two immiscible liquid layers in an extraction
options.D: Dispensing a measured volume of indicator to a conical flask

questions.explanation: The thistle funnel allows addition of acid dropwise to the solid reactant while keeping the gas-generation apparatus sealed, controlling the rate of gas production.

questions.stem: In a titration set-up, why is a white tile or sheet of white paper placed beneath the conical flask?

options.A: To prevent the flask from sliding or moving during swirling
options.B: To keep the flask and its contents warm during the reaction
options.C: To provide a sharp, bright white background making the colour change at the endpoint easier to detect
options.D: To reflect heat from below and maintain a steady reaction temperature

questions.explanation: The white background maximises contrast at the titration endpoint, helping the analyst detect the precise moment of permanent colour change.

questions.stem: Which piece of apparatus is specifically designed for evaporating liquid solutions to dryness or concentrating them?

options.A: Evaporating dish
options.B: Beaker
options.C: Crucible
options.D: Watch glass

questions.explanation: The evaporating dish is made of porcelain and can be heated directly on a wire gauze. Its shallow design allows rapid evaporation of solvent.

options.A: Measuring approximate volumes for rough experiments

options.C: Transferring a fixed definite volume from a stock solution

options.A: Hydrogen gas (H₂) from a cylinder
options.B: Oxygen gas (O₂) under pressure

options.A: Measuring volumes of liquids accurately
options.B: Supporting filter paper during gravity filtration
options.C: Holding solid substances being heated or ignited to very high temperatures

questions.explanation: Crucibles are made of porcelain, clay, or platinum and can withstand extremely high temperatures needed for ignition and decomposition reactions.

options.A: Measuring the pH of a solution accurately
options.B: Grinding and crushing solid chemicals into a fine, homogeneous powder

questions.explanation: The pestle is used to crush and grind solids in the bowl (mortar), increasing surface area for faster dissolution or reaction.

options.A: To filter fine solid particles from a liquid suspension
options.B: To collect gases over water by displacement
options.C: To support a vessel and distribute heat evenly from the Bunsen burner below
options.D: To weigh solid chemicals accurately on an analytical balance

questions.explanation: The ceramic centre of the wire gauze spreads heat from the Bunsen flame uniformly, preventing hot spots that could crack glassware.

options.A: A measuring cylinder is more accurate than a burette

options.C: A burette (±0.05 cm³) is far more accurate than a measuring cylinder (±0.5 mL); only the burette has a stopcock

options.B: Electrolyzing water to produce and separately collect hydrogen (cathode) and oxygen (anode) in graduated tubes
